# 2021 年 12 月六级真题解析〔第二套〕

# Part II > Listening Comprehension

# Section A

# Conversation One

# ·听力原文·

W: Hi, David. I haven't seen you in class for almost two weeks. We thought you had disappeared on holiday early or something.

M: Hi, Sarah. Well, it's a bit of a long story, I'm afraid. I got a throat infection last week and had to go to the hospital to get some antibiotics, as I really wasn't getting any better.

W: Oh, yeah. There have been so many viruses going around this winter. The weather's been so awful for the last few weeks.

M: [1] And on the way back from the hospital, I slipped on some ice and fell, and then had to go to the hospital to get an X-ray, because I basically thought I'd broken my wrist. Although, thankfully, it's not broken. But I need to be careful with it for the next few weeks.

W: Oh, that's too bad. How unfortunate.

M: To make things worse, I managed to fall right in front of four girls from the ninth grade. So I was utterly humiliated. Plus, the laptop in my bag was broken, too.

W: Now, what a complete catastrophe. [2] Is the laptop still under warranty? If it is, then you can easily send it back to the manufacturer, and they'll send you a brand new one for free, surely.

M: The warranty ran out three days before I broke it, and all my essays are in there. And I need to hand them in before we break for the Christmas holidays.

W: Listen, [3] I have the number of a really good affordable computer repair shop at home. My dad has used this guy before, and he can work miracles. [4] Let's go back to my house, and we can call the repair shop. And you can have some tea and cookies, too.

M: Wow, thanks, Sarah. That would be great. Let me just call my mom and let her know I'll be home a little bit later.

# Conversation Two

# ·听力原文·

M: Welcome to this week's episode of Book Talk. With me today is Heidi Brown, [5] a historian who has written five critically acclaimed books about military history.

W: Thanks for having me, John. I'm so excited to talk about my latest book, which was published last month.

M: So this book is a novel, your first attempt at that genre, and thus a bit of a departure for you.

W: [6] I'd say it's a major departure, as it's not just a work of fiction. It's set 200 years in the future.

M: Right. So how did that happen? You spent three decades writing about the past and focusing on the 18th and 19th centuries. And now you're speculating about the future.

W: After years of researching soldiers and chronicling their lives during battle, I just started wondering about other facets of their lives, especially their personal lives.

M: I can see that. Your novel is about soldiers, but it focuses on their relationships, especially the bonds between sons and mothers and men and their wives.

W: Yes. That focus came about when I still intended to write another book of history. [7] I started by researching soldiers' actual personal lives, studying their letters home.

M: So how did that history book become a novel?

W: Well, I realized that the historical record was incomplete, so I'd either have to leave a lot of gaps or make a lot more assumptions than a historian should.

M: But why write a novel set in the future when your credentials are perfect for a historical novel? As a historian, any historical novel you write would have a lot of credibility.

W: [8] I felt too constrained working with the past, like what I wrote needed to be fact as opposed to fiction. But writing about the future gave me more freedom to imagine and invent.

M: Having read your book, I'm glad you made that choice to move into fiction.

# Section B

# Passage One

# ·听力原文·

Whether it's being held by a polar bear or Santa Claus, the characteristic Coca-Cola glass bottle appears in nearly all of the company's advertisements. [9] Most Americans no longer drink Coke from the glass bottle, but the company celebrated the bottle's 100th anniversary. It has been sold in more than 200 countries. In 1915, a bottle of Coke cost a nickel. As the drink grew popular, it faced many competitors and counterfeits trying to copy its logo. [10] Coca-Cola historian Ted Ryan explains the company sought packaging that couldn't be duplicated. A request went out to eight glass makers. Workers at the Root Glass Company searched an encyclopedia at their local library and found the cocoa seed — not an ingredient of the soda. [11] They designed the bottle after the shape of the cocoa seed, with an enlarged middle. It won over Coke executives in Atlanta, received its own trademark, spurred collections, and became an iconic part of American culture. The bottle earned a patent 100 years ago. By World War II, sales had reached billions. Americans mostly use aluminum or plastic today, but the glass bottle remains a globally recognized American symbol.

# Passage Two

# ·听力原文·

[12] Research shows that a few moments of conversation with a stranger creates a measurable improvement in mood. Yet most people are reluctant to initiate because they assume the opposite. In an experiment, commuters who talked to nearby strangers found their commute more enjoyable, though most predicted solitude would be more pleasant. [13] Social anxiety is identified as the problem — people underestimate others' interest in connecting. They assume strangers don't want to converse and never start talking. Only those forced to chat by the experiment discovered how pleasant it could be. Human beings are social animals, and those who misunderstand social interactions' impact may not be social enough for their own well-being. You may occasionally have a negative encounter that sticks in memory because [14] the human brain is biased toward dwelling on negative events. But starting conversations is still worth the risk of rejection. Conversing with strangers makes them happier too — [15] the pleasure of connection seems contagious. People who are spoken to have equally positive experiences as those who initiate conversation.

# Section C

# Recording One

# ·听力原文·

[16] The Caribbean islands are divided into two worlds, a rich one and a poor one. This tropical region's economy is based mainly on farming. Farmers are of two types. One is the plantation owner who may have hundreds of thousands of acres. In contrast, the small cultivator is working only a few acres of land. Most visitors to the Caribbean are rich like the plantation owner. They do not realize or do not want to realize that many foreign families barely manage to get by on what they grow.

The Caribbean produces many things. [17] Sugar is the main product. Other export crops are tobacco, coffee, bananas, spices, and citrus fruits, such as orange, lemon or grapefruit. From the West Indies also come oil, mineral pitch and many forest products. Jamaica's aluminum ore supplies are the world's largest. Oil comes from Trinidad, Aruba and Curaçao. But for many of the smaller islands, sugar is the only export. Rum, a strong alcoholic drink which is distilled from sugar cane, is also an export.

The world's best rum comes from this area. Local kinds vary from the light rums of Puerto Rico to the heavier dark rums of Barbados and Jamaica. American tourists enjoy stocking up on inexpensive, high quality Caribbean rum while they are on vacation. In Curaçao, the well-known liquor of that name is made from the thick outer skin of a native orange. Ever since America's colonial days, Caribbean islands have been favorite places to visit. Since World War Two, tourism has increased rapidly because great numbers of people go there. The islanders have built elaborate resorts, developed harbors and airfields, improved beaches and have expanded sea and air routes.

Everything is at the resort — hotel, beach, shopping and recreation. The vacationer never has any reason to explore the island. As in most places, those who have money live well indeed; those who don't have money live at various levels of poverty. [18] But here the poor greatly outnumber the wealthy. A visitor will find rich people living in apartments or Spanish houses at the seaside or in the countryside. Their servants might include a cook, a maid and a nurse for the children. Most of the people live well below the poverty level. In towns, they live crowded together in tiny houses. Islanders make the best they can of what they have. Their homes are quite shabby. Sadly, most tourists never see this side of the Caribbean.

# Recording Two

# ·听力原文·

Talk to anyone who's a generation or two older and they would most likely comment that children are more spoiled these days. No one wants to have or be around demanding, selfish and spoiled children — those who get bad-tempered or silently brood when they're not given everything they want immediately. Paradoxically, the parents of such children encouraged this demanding behavior in the mistaken belief that by giving their children everything they can, their children will be happy. In the short term, perhaps they are right. [19] But in the longer term, such children end up lonely, dependent, chronically dissatisfied and resentful of the parents who tried so hard to please them.

Undoubtedly parents want to raise happy children who are confident, capable and likable rather than spoiled and miserable. [20] One factor hindering this is that parents can't or don't spend enough quality time with their kids and substitute this deficit with toys, games, gadgets, and the like. Rather than getting material things, children need parents' devoted attention. The quantity of time spent together is less important than the content of that time.

Instead of instantly satisfying their wishes, parents should help them work out a plan to earn things they'd like to have. This teaches them to value the effort as well as what it achieved, and allows them to enjoy anticipation. Numerous psychological studies have demonstrated that children who learn to wait for things they desire are more likely to succeed in a number of ways later in life. One famous experiment in the 1960s involved three- to six-year-old children. They were given a choice between receiving a small reward such as a cookie immediately, or if they waited 15 minutes, they could have two. Follow-up studies have found that those who chose to delay satisfaction are now more academically successful, have greater self-worth and even tend to be healthier.

If they fail, children should be encouraged to keep trying rather than to give up if they really want the desired result. [21] This teaches them how to handle and recover from disappointment, which is associated with greater success and satisfaction academically, financially and in personal relationships. And lastly, parents should encourage their children to look at life from other points of view as well as their own. This teaches them to be understanding of and sympathetic towards others — qualities that should take them a long way in life.

# Recording Three

# ·听力原文·

[22] It's not hard to mess up an interview. Most people feel nervous sitting across from a hiring manager, answering questions that effectively open themselves up for judgment. And your chances of being more carefully considered for the job can quickly go downhill just by saying the wrong thing at the wrong time.

[23] The most obvious thing not to do is complain. Employers want to hire positive people. Talking about a previous job negatively raises concerns that you might be difficult to manage, or you might be someone that blames management for your own poor performance. Don't say that you've moved around in jobs because you haven't found the right fit or feel that you were not challenged enough. Statements like these will make you sound aimless and lost. An interviewer may well think: why would this role be any different for you? You will probably leave here in six months. It also begs the question of what type of relationship you had with your manager. It doesn't sound like you had open communication with him or her.

[24] Managers usually love people who can self-sustain and enable growth through taking initiative, who are strong at following through on their work and who bring ideas and solutions to the table. If you were in a management or leadership position, when discussing your current role, never take all the credit for accomplishments or achievements. Emphasize your team and how, through their talents, your vision was realized. Most successful leaders know that they are only as good as their team. And acknowledging this in an interview will go a long way towards suggesting that you might be the right person for the position you are applying for.

Lastly, have a good idea of what your role will be and try to convey the idea that you're flexible. Asking what your role will be suggests you will limit yourself purely to what is expected of you. In reality, your role is whatever you make of it. [25] This is especially true in small companies where the ability to adapt and take on new responsibilities is highly valued. And this is equally important if you are just starting out. Entry-level interviewees would do well to demonstrate a broad set of skills in most interviews. It's important to have a wide skill set as many start-ups and small companies are moving really fast. Employers are looking for candidates that are intelligent and can quickly adapt and excel in a growing company.

paragraphs.translation: 世界上最好的朗姆酒就产自这个地区。当地的朗姆酒品种多种多样，从波多黎各的淡朗姆酒到巴巴多斯和牙买加的浓烈黑朗姆酒。美国游客在度假时喜欢储备廉价、优质的加勒比朗姆酒。在库拉索岛，著名的同名酒是由当地橙子的厚外皮制成的。自美国殖民时代以来，加勒比岛屿一直是最受欢迎的旅游胜地。自第二次世界大战以来，旅游业迅速发展，因为有大量的人前往那里。岛民建造了精致的度假村，开发了港口和机场，改善了海滩，并扩大了海上和空中航线。

paragraphs.text: Everything is at the resort — hotel, beach, shopping and recreation. The vacationer never has any reason to explore the island. As in most places, those who have money live well indeed; those who don't have money live at various levels of poverty. But here the poor greatly outnumber the wealthy. A visitor will find rich people living in apartments or Spanish houses at the seaside or in the countryside. Their servants might include a cook, a maid and a nurse for the children. Most of the people live well below the poverty level. In towns, they live crowded together in tiny houses. Islanders make the best they can of what they have. Their homes are quite shabby. Sadly, most tourists never see this side of the Caribbean.
paragraphs.translation: 一切都在度假村里——酒店、海滩、购物和娱乐。度假者从来没有任何理由去探索这个岛屿。和大多数地方一样，有钱的人确实过得很好；有钱的人确实过得很好。那些没有钱的人生活在不同程度的贫困中。但在这里，穷人的数量远远多于富人。游客会发现富人住在海边或乡村的公寓或西班牙房屋中。他们的仆人可能包括一名厨师、一名女佣和一名照顾孩子的护士。大多数人生活在贫困线以下。在城镇里，他们挤在一起住在小房子里。岛民充分利用他们所拥有的一切。他们的家相当破旧。可悲的是，大多数游客从未见过加勒比海的这一面。

paragraphs.text: Talk to anyone who's a generation or two older and they would most likely comment that children are more spoiled these days. No one wants to have or be around demanding, selfish and spoiled children — those who get bad-tempered or silently brood when they're not given everything they want immediately. Paradoxically, the parents of such children encouraged this demanding behavior in the mistaken belief that by giving their children everything they can, their children will be happy. In the short term, perhaps they are right. But in the longer term, such children end up lonely, dependent, chronically dissatisfied and resentful of the parents who tried so hard to please them.
paragraphs.translation: 与年长一两代的人交谈，他们很可能会说现在的孩子更被宠坏了。没有人愿意拥有一个要求高、自私、被宠坏的孩子，或者和他们在一起——这些孩子如果没有立即得到他们想要的一切，就会变得脾气暴躁或者默默地忧郁。矛盾的是，这些孩子的父母鼓励这种苛求的行为，因为他们错误地认为，只要给孩子力所能及的一切，他们的孩子就会快乐。从短期来看，也许他们是对的。但从长远来看，这些孩子最终会变得孤独、依赖、长期对竭尽全力取悦他们的父母感到不满和怨恨。

paragraphs.text: Undoubtedly parents want to raise happy children who are confident, capable and likable rather than spoiled and miserable. One factor hindering this is that parents can't or don't spend enough quality time with their kids and substitute this deficit with toys, games, gadgets, and the like. Rather than getting material things, children need parents' devoted attention. The quantity of time spent together is less important than the content of that time.
paragraphs.translation: 毫无疑问，父母希望培养出自信、有能力、讨人喜欢的快乐孩子，而不是被宠坏、痛苦的孩子。阻碍这一点的一个因素是父母不能或没有花足够的时间陪伴孩子，并用玩具、游戏、小玩意等来弥补这一缺陷。孩子需要的不是物质上的满足，而是父母的全心投入。在一起度过的时间的长短并不重要，重要的是时间的内容。

paragraphs.text: Instead of instantly satisfying their wishes, parents should help them work out a plan to earn things they'd like to have. This teaches them to value the effort as well as what it achieved, and allows them to enjoy anticipation. Numerous psychological studies have demonstrated that children who learn to wait for things they desire are more likely to succeed in a number of ways later in life. One famous experiment in the 1960s involved three- to six-year-old children. They were given a choice between receiving a small reward such as a cookie immediately, or if they waited 15 minutes, they could have two. Follow-up studies have found that those who chose to delay satisfaction are now more academically successful, have greater self-worth and even tend to be healthier.
paragraphs.translation: 父母不应该立即满足他们的愿望，而应该帮助他们制定一个计划来赚取他们想要拥有的东西。这教会他们重视努力以及所取得的成果，并让他们享受期待。大量心理学研究表明，学会等待自己想要的东西的孩子在以后的生活中更有可能在许多方面取得成功。 20 世纪 60 年代的一项著名实验涉及三到六岁的儿童。他们可以选择立即获得一块饼干等小奖励，或者等待 15 分钟就可以得到两块。后续研究发现，那些选择延迟满足的人现在在学业上更成功，有更高的自我价值，甚至往往更健康。

paragraphs.text: If they fail, children should be encouraged to keep trying rather than to give up if they really want the desired result. This teaches them how to handle and recover from disappointment, which is associated with greater success and satisfaction academically, financially and in personal relationships. And lastly, parents should encourage their children to look at life from other points of view as well as their own. This teaches them to be understanding of and sympathetic towards others — qualities that should take them a long way in life.
paragraphs.translation: 如果失败了，如果孩子真的想要想要的结果，应该鼓励他们继续尝试而不是放弃。这教会他们如何处理失望并从中恢复，这与学业、经济和人际关系方面的更大成功和满意度相关。最后，父母应该鼓励孩子从自己的角度和其他角度看待生活。这教会他们理解和同情他人——这些品质应该会让他们在人生的道路上走得更远。

paragraphs.text: It's not hard to mess up an interview. Most people feel nervous sitting across from a hiring manager, answering questions that effectively open themselves up for judgment. And your chances of being more carefully considered for the job can quickly go downhill just by saying the wrong thing at the wrong time.
paragraphs.translation: 搞砸面试并不难。大多数人坐在招聘经理对面，回答那些让自己容易受到评判的问题，都会感到紧张。如果你在错误的时间说了错误的话，那么你被更仔细地考虑这份工作的机会就会很快下降。

paragraphs.text: The most obvious thing not to do is complain. Employers want to hire positive people. Talking about a previous job negatively raises concerns that you might be difficult to manage, or you might be someone that blames management for your own poor performance. Don't say that you've moved around in jobs because you haven't found the right fit or feel that you were not challenged enough. Statements like these will make you sound aimless and lost. An interviewer may well think: why would this role be any different for you? You will probably leave here in six months. It also begs the question of what type of relationship you had with your manager. It doesn't sound like you had open communication with him or her.
paragraphs.translation: 最明显不要做的事情就是抱怨。雇主希望雇用积极的人。消极地谈论以前的工作会让人担心你可能难以管理，或者你可能会因为自己的糟糕表现而责怪管理层。不要说你换工作是因为你还没有找到合适的人选，或者觉得自己没有受到足够的挑战。诸如此类的言论会让你听起来漫无目的、迷失方向。面试官可能会想：为什么这个角色对你来说会有什么不同？你可能会在六个月后离开这里。它还引出了您与经理之间的关系类型的问题。听起来你并没有与他或她进行公开的沟通。

paragraphs.text: Managers usually love people who can self-sustain and enable growth through taking initiative, who are strong at following through on their work and who bring ideas and solutions to the table. If you were in a management or leadership position, when discussing your current role, never take all the credit for accomplishments or achievements. Emphasize your team and how, through their talents, your vision was realized. Most successful leaders know that they are only as good as their team. And acknowledging this in an interview will go a long way towards suggesting that you might be the right person for the position you are applying for.
paragraphs.translation: 经理通常喜欢那些能够自我维持并通过主动行动实现成长的人，他们能够坚强地完成工作并提出想法和解决方案。如果您担任管理或领导职位，在讨论您当前的角色时，切勿将所有成就或成就归功于自己。强调您的团队以及如何通过他们的才能实现您的愿景。大多数成功的领导者都知道，他们的表现取决于他们的团队。在面试中承认这一点将有助于表明您可能是您所申请职位的合适人选。

paragraphs.text: Lastly, have a good idea of what your role will be and try to convey the idea that you're flexible. Asking what your role will be suggests you will limit yourself purely to what is expected of you. In reality, your role is whatever you make of it. This is especially true in small companies where the ability to adapt and take on new responsibilities is highly valued. And this is equally important if you are just starting out. Entry-level interviewees would do well to demonstrate a broad set of skills in most interviews. It's important to have a wide skill set as many start-ups and small companies are moving really fast. Employers are looking for candidates that are intelligent and can quickly adapt and excel in a growing company.
paragraphs.translation: 最后，充分了解您的角色，并尝试传达您灵活的想法。询问你的角色将意味着你将纯粹限制自己于对你的期望。事实上，你的角色取决于你的角色。对于小公司来说尤其如此，因为它们高度重视适应和承担新责任的能力。如果您刚刚起步，这一点同样重要。在大多数面试中，入门级面试者最好能展示出广泛的技能。拥有广泛的技能非常重要，因为许多初创企业和小公司发展得非常快。雇主正在寻找聪明、能够快速适应并在成长型公司中脱颖而出的候选人。

sentences.translation: 我很高兴谈论我上个月出版的最新书。
sentences.paragraphTranslation: 女：谢谢你邀请我，约翰。我很高兴谈论我上个月出版的最新书。

sentences.speaker: M
sentences.text: So this book is a novel, your first attempt at that genre, and thus a bit of a departure for you.
sentences.translation: 男：所以这本书是一本小说，是你第一次尝试这种类型，因此对你来说有点不同。

sentences.speaker: W
sentences.text: I'd say it's a major departure, as it's not just a work of fiction.
sentences.translation: 我想说这是一个重大的转变，因为它不仅仅是一部小说。
sentences.paragraphTranslation: 女：我想说这是一个重大的转变，因为它不仅仅是一部虚构的作品。故事设定在200年后的未来。

sentences.speaker: W
sentences.text: It's set 200 years in the future.
sentences.translation: 故事设定在200年后的未来。
sentences.paragraphTranslation: 女：我想说这是一个重大的转变，因为它不仅仅是一部虚构的作品。故事设定在200年后的未来。

sentences.speaker: M
sentences.text: Right.
sentences.translation: 对。
sentences.paragraphTranslation: 男：对。那么这是怎么发生的呢？您花了三十年的时间来写过去，重点关注 18 世纪和 19 世纪。现在你正在猜测未来。

sentences.speaker: M
sentences.text: So how did that happen?
sentences.translation: 那么这是怎么发生的呢？
sentences.paragraphTranslation: 男：对。那么这是怎么发生的呢？您花了三十年的时间来写过去，重点关注 18 世纪和 19 世纪。现在你正在猜测未来。

sentences.speaker: M
sentences.text: You spent three decades writing about the past and focusing on the 18th and 19th centuries.
sentences.translation: 您花了三十年的时间来写过去，重点关注 18 世纪和 19 世纪。
sentences.paragraphTranslation: 男：对。那么这是怎么发生的呢？您花了三十年的时间来写过去，重点关注 18 世纪和 19 世纪。现在你正在猜测未来。

sentences.speaker: M
sentences.text: And now you're speculating about the future.
sentences.translation: 现在你正在猜测未来。
sentences.paragraphTranslation: 男：对。那么这是怎么发生的呢？您花了三十年的时间来写过去，重点关注 18 世纪和 19 世纪。现在你正在猜测未来。

sentences.text: After years of researching soldiers and chronicling their lives during battle, I just started wondering about other facets of their lives, especially their personal lives.
sentences.translation: 女：经过多年研究士兵并记录他们在战斗中的生活后，我开始想知道他们生活的其他方面，尤其是他们的个人生活。

sentences.speaker: M
sentences.text: I can see that.
sentences.translation: 我看得出来。
sentences.paragraphTranslation: 男：我看得出来。你的小说是关于士兵的，但它关注的是他们的关系，尤其是儿子与母亲、男人与妻子之间的纽带。

sentences.speaker: M
sentences.text: Your novel is about soldiers, but it focuses on their relationships, especially the bonds between sons and mothers and men and their wives.
sentences.translation: 你的小说是关于士兵的，但它关注的是他们的关系，尤其是儿子与母亲、男人与妻子之间的纽带。

sentences.speaker: W
sentences.text: Yes.
sentences.translation: 是的。
sentences.paragraphTranslation: 女：是的。当我仍打算写另一本历史书时，这个焦点就出现了。我首先研究士兵的实际个人生活，研究他们的家信。

sentences.speaker: W
sentences.text: That focus came about when I still intended to write another book of history.
sentences.translation: 当我仍打算写另一本历史书时，这个焦点就出现了。
sentences.paragraphTranslation: 女：是的。当我仍打算写另一本历史书时，这个焦点就出现了。我首先研究士兵的实际个人生活，研究他们的家信。

sentences.speaker: W
sentences.text: I started by researching soldiers' actual personal lives, studying their letters home.
sentences.translation: 我首先研究士兵的实际个人生活，研究他们的家信。
sentences.paragraphTranslation: 女：是的。当我仍打算写另一本历史书时，这个焦点就出现了。我首先研究士兵的实际个人生活，研究他们的家信。

sentences.text: So how did that history book become a novel?
sentences.translation: 男：那么那本历史书是怎么变成小说的呢？

sentences.speaker: W
sentences.text: Well, I realized that the historical record was incomplete, so I'd either have to leave a lot of gaps or make a lot more assumptions than a historian should.
sentences.translation: 女：嗯，我意识到历史记录是不完整的，所以我要么必须留下很多空白，要么做出比历史学家应该做的更多的假设。

sentences.text: But why write a novel set in the future when your credentials are perfect for a historical novel?
sentences.translation: 但是，当你的资历非常适合写历史小说时，为什么要写一部以未来为背景的小说呢？
sentences.paragraphTranslation: 男：但是当你的资历非常适合写历史小说时，为什么要写一部以未来为背景的小说呢？作为一名历史学家，你写的任何历史小说都会有很大的可信度。

sentences.speaker: M
sentences.text: As a historian, any historical novel you write would have a lot of credibility.
sentences.translation: 作为一名历史学家，你写的任何历史小说都会有很大的可信度。
sentences.paragraphTranslation: 男：但是当你的资历非常适合写历史小说时，为什么要写一部以未来为背景的小说呢？作为一名历史学家，你写的任何历史小说都会有很大的可信度。

sentences.text: I felt too constrained working with the past, like what I wrote needed to be fact as opposed to fiction.

sentences.paragraphTranslation: 女：我觉得与过去打交道太受限制了，就像我写的东西必须是事实而不是虚构的。但写下未来给了我更多的想象和发明的自由。

sentences.text: But writing about the future gave me more freedom to imagine and invent.

sentences.paragraphTranslation: 女：我觉得与过去打交道太受限制了，就像我写的东西必须是事实而不是虚构的。但写下未来给了我更多的想象和发明的自由。

sentences.text: Talk to anyone who's a generation or two older and they would most likely comment that children are more spoiled these days.

sentences.paragraphTranslation: 与年长一两代的人交谈，他们很可能会说现在的孩子更被宠坏了。没有人愿意拥有一个要求高、自私、被宠坏的孩子，或者和他们在一起——这些孩子如果没有立即得到他们想要的一切，就会变得脾气暴躁或者默默地忧郁。矛盾的是，这些孩子的父母鼓励这种苛求的行为，因为他们错误地认为，只要给孩子力所能及的一切，他们的孩子就会快乐。从短期来看，也许他们是对的。但从长远来看，这些孩子最终会变得孤独、依赖、长期对竭尽全力取悦他们的父母感到不满和怨恨。

sentences.text: Instead of instantly satisfying their wishes, parents should help them work out a plan to earn things they'd like to have.
sentences.translation: 父母不应该立即满足他们的愿望，而应该帮助他们制定一个计划来赚取他们想要拥有的东西。
sentences.paragraphTranslation: 父母不应该立即满足他们的愿望，而应该帮助他们制定一个计划来赚取他们想要拥有的东西。这教会他们重视努力以及所取得的成果，并让他们享受期待。大量心理学研究表明，学会等待自己想要的东西的孩子在以后的生活中更有可能在许多方面取得成功。 20 世纪 60 年代的一项著名实验涉及三到六岁的儿童。他们可以选择立即获得一块饼干等小奖励，或者等待 15 分钟就可以得到两块。后续研究发现，那些选择延迟满足的人现在在学业上更成功，有更高的自我价值，甚至往往更健康。
